alex: Heads-up: Saturday 03:00 UTC we'll run a thermal-probe + NIC microcode swap on the "satellite" rack cohort in apac-east1. Plan is rolling cordon -> drain -> soft reboot -> nic microcode apply -> warmback. Expect transient 8-12% GPU capacity drop in that region, ~90m window but we'll stage to ~40m per cohort to reduce impact.

maria: how many racks / how many tenant pools affected? any dedicated customers impacted?

alex: 3 racks (sat-01..03), they host a mix of hosted + a couple of small dedicated pools (reserved: pool-d-sat). Dedicated tenants notif'd via email; we'll shift their routes to apac-east2 standby pool during windows. Hosted requests will be routed by policy to nearby pools (apac-east2, apac-west1) automatically.

sam: what's the fallback path if KV cache warmup fails and we see latency spike?

alex: fallback plan:
- abort stage -> roll back microcode on that rack
- fail open routing to apac-east2 / apac-west1
- enable aggressive prefix-cache seeding on standby pools
- if sustained issues >15m, run canary rollback to previous fw across sat-01 and re-evaluate

jordan: can we get a quick cost estimate for the route spill? want to pre-approve temporary burst capacity charges.

alex: rough numbers: expected extra cross-region token egress ~120k tokens/hr during peak => ~$30/hr for the maintenance window. If we need burst VMs/reserved warm nodes it's an extra ~$150/hr worst-case. I'll attach breakdown after canary.

maria: runbook link?

alex: infra runbook (short):

```
# sat-thermal-probe runbook (short)
1) /bin/ops sched --cohort sat-01 --hold 20m
2) kubectl cordon node=<rack-nodes>
3) kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node=... 
4) infra-tool apply-nic-fw --version v1.2.3 --nodes sat-01
5) reboot nodes, wait for healthchecks
6) validate: 99th latency < baseline+25ms, token rate within 10%
7) uncordon
```

alex: canaries: sat-01 small subset of nodes first (~20% of rack). We'll run perf-probe job: `bench/infer --model rdl-3b --qps 0.5 --seq 512` and watch p50/p95/p99 for 15m.

infra-bot: Reminder set for 2024-11-02 03:00 UTC — sat-thermal-probe maintenance

alex: yes, routing policy is tier-aware: for affinity=true tenants we'll avoid cross-region unless capacity <10% of their SLA threshold. For those tenants we'll pre-warm prefix cache on their standby pool 30m before start.

maria: can you add a quick blurb for support so CS can triage any reported latency spikes?

If customer sees >15m sustained degradation, escalate to eng-infra oncall and include request id + sample logs."
